entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-4xjf-493q-98p3: Gitea SSH Key Parser Denial of Service
entry.content:
Gitea SSH Key Parser Denial of Service

Aliases: CVE-2026-56657, GO-2026-6042

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • code.gitea.io/gitea — fixed in 1.27.0

Gitea's SSH key ingestion endpoint accepts keys in RFC 4716 (SSH2) format and normalises them before storage. The normalisation function contains an O(N²) string concatenation loop with no input size limit, meaning a single malicious key submission can force the server to perform an amount of work that grows quadratically with the size of the input. Any authenticated user can exploit this to exhaust the server's CPU and memory, taking the instance offline. ### Root Cause An attacker sends a POST /api/v1/user/keys request with a Bearer token and a JSON body whose key field contains a malicious RFC 4716 (SSH2) public key.
